scan.summary: This is Oregon DEQ's Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit (ACDP). It allows the Portland facility to run two acid/caustic scrubbers and four solvent tanks that vent to a carbon unit. Because it is the agency's own document, there is nothing in it for you to fix. What matters is keeping the daily, weekly, quarterly and annual monitoring records, filing the reports on time, and getting it renewed. It expires on November 15, 2026, 47 days from today. The renewal application was due July 18, 2026, which has already passed, so the first thing to check is whether a complete renewal application went in by that date.
scan.freshness_note: Issued September 1, 2021, and expires November 15, 2026, 47 days from today. Condition 1.3 required a complete renewal application by July 18, 2026. If you filed on time, you may keep operating under this permit until DEQ acts, so keep proof of the filing date with the permit. If nothing was filed, contact Oregon DEQ Northwest Region right away. Condition 1.2 says running the sources after expiry without a renewed permit or a timely renewal application violates the permit. Once DEQ issues the renewed permit, replace this copy with it.

conditions.title: Operate the sources in Section 2 under all permit conditions and all applicable DEQ rules
conditions.evidence_expected: The permit on file plus the monitoring and reporting records listed below.

conditions.title: Do not run the permitted sources after November 15, 2026, without a renewed permit or a timely renewal application
conditions.evidence_expected: The renewed permit, or proof of a timely renewal application.

conditions.title: Submit a complete renewal application on or before July 18, 2026 (120 days before expiry)
conditions.evidence_expected: A copy of the submitted renewal application and DEQ's receipt or acknowledgment showing a date on or before July 18, 2026.

conditions.title: Notify DEQ in writing at least 60 days before any change in ownership, and before any source modification that would increase emissions
conditions.evidence_expected: Copies of written notices to DEQ, or a note that no ownership change or modification occurred.

conditions.title: Keep pressure drop across scrubbers S-1 and S-2 between 2.0 and 6.0 in. water column while their lines operate, and record it once per operating day
conditions.evidence_expected: A scrubber log with daily pressure-drop readings for S-1 and S-2 on every operating day.

conditions.title: Inspect each scrubber's recirculation pump, spray nozzles, packing and mist eliminator at least once per calendar quarter
conditions.evidence_expected: Quarterly scrubber log entries showing the date, the inspector and any corrective action.

conditions.title: Replace the carbon in unit C-1 at least every 12 months, or sooner if the weekly detector-tube check at the C-1 outlet shows breakthrough
conditions.evidence_expected: Weekly detector-tube check records and carbon replacement records (dates, vendor invoices or manifests).

conditions.title: Keep visible emissions from any permitted source at or below 20% opacity, except for periods totaling no more than three minutes in any hour
conditions.evidence_expected: Visible-emissions observation records, or no-visible-emissions notes, and any excess-emission reports.

conditions.title: Submit an annual report by February 15 covering the prior calendar year
conditions.evidence_expected: Submitted annual reports with throughput by line, scrubber log summaries, carbon replacement dates and excess emission events.

conditions.title: Submit a semi-annual monitoring report by July 31 covering January through June
conditions.evidence_expected: Submitted semi-annual reports, including the one due July 31, 2026, with proof of submittal.

conditions.title: Keep all records the permit requires for at least five years and make them available to DEQ
conditions.evidence_expected: An organized five-year record archive (logs, reports, carbon records).

conditions.title: Minimize emissions during scrubber malfunction, including stopping the associated repackaging line
conditions.evidence_expected: Malfunction and shutdown records in the scrubber log.

conditions.title: Notify DEQ within 24 hours of discovering any deviation, and send a written report within 15 days
conditions.evidence_expected: Deviation notification emails or call logs, plus the 15-day written reports.

conditions.title: Pay the annual permit fee by the invoice due date
conditions.evidence_expected: DEQ fee invoices and proof of payment.

STATE OF OREGON
DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY
Northwest Region · 700 NE Multnomah Street, Suite 600, Portland, Oregon
97232
STANDARD AIR CONTAMINANT DISCHARGE PERMIT
Issued under OAR 340-216
Permit number: 26-2841-ST-01
Permittee: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, LLC
Facility: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, Portland Facility
Facility address: 4410 NW Front Avenue, Portland, Oregon 97210
Source category: Chemical storage and repackaging with vapor control
Date issued: September 1, 2021
Expiration date: November 15, 2026
This permit is issued in accordance with the provisions of ORS 468A.040 and OAR 340-216 and
authorizes the permittee to operate the air contaminant sources described below at the facility address,
subject to the conditions of this permit.
SECTION 1. GENERAL CONDITIONS
1.1 The permittee shall operate the sources listed in Section 2 in compliance with all conditions of this
permit and all applicable rules of the Department.
1.2 This permit expires on November 15, 2026. Operation of the permitted sources after the expiration
date without a renewed permit or a timely renewal application is a violation of this permit.
1.3 The permittee shall submit a complete application for renewal of this permit no later than 120 days
before the expiration date, that is, on or before July 18, 2026. A permittee that submits a timely and
complete renewal application may continue to operate under the terms of this permit until the Department
takes final action on the application.
1.4 The permittee shall notify the Department in writing at least 60 days before any change in ownership,
and before any modification to a permitted source that would increase emissions of any regulated
pollutant.
SECTION 2. PERMITTED SOURCES
2.1 Packed-bed wet scrubber S-1 serving the acid repackaging line (design flow 4,500 scfm).
2.2 Packed-bed wet scrubber S-2 serving the caustic repackaging line (design flow 3,000 scfm).
2.3 Solvent storage tanks T-3, T-4, T-5 and T-6 (each 10,000 gallons, fixed roof, vented to carbon
adsorption unit C-1).
SECTION 3. OPERATING AND MONITORING CONDITIONS
3.1 The permittee shall maintain the pressure drop across each scrubber S-1 and S-2 within the range of
2.0 to 6.0 inches of water column whenever the associated line is operating, and shall record the pressure
drop reading once per operating day in a scrubber log.
3.2 The permittee shall inspect each scrubber's recirculation pump, spray nozzles, packing and mist
eliminator at least once per calendar quarter and record the date, the inspector and any corrective action in
the scrubber log.
3.3 The permittee shall replace the carbon in adsorption unit C-1 at least once every 12 months or when
breakthrough is detected by the weekly detector-tube check at the C-1 outlet, whichever comes first, and
shall record each replacement.
3.4 Visible emissions from any permitted source shall not exceed 20 percent opacity for any period
aggregating more than three minutes in any one hour.
SECTION 4. RECORDKEEPING AND REPORTING
4.1 The permittee shall submit an annual report to the Department by February 15 of each year covering
the previous calendar year, including total throughput by line, scrubber log summaries, carbon
replacement dates and any excess emission events.
4.2 The permittee shall submit a semi-annual monitoring report by July 31 covering January through June
of the same year.
4.3 The permittee shall keep all records required by this permit for at least five years from the date of the
record and make them available to the Department on request.
SECTION 5. EXCESS EMISSIONS AND UPSETS
5.1 The permittee shall take all reasonable steps to minimize emissions during any period of scrubber
malfunction, including stopping the associated repackaging line until the scrubber is returned to service.
5.2 The permittee shall notify the Department by telephone or email within 24 hours of discovering any
deviation from a condition of this permit, and shall submit a written report within 15 days describing the
deviation, its cause, its duration and the corrective action taken.
SECTION 6. ADMINISTRATIVE
6.1 This permit may be modified, suspended or revoked for cause, including violation of any condition,
obtaining the permit by misrepresentation, or a change in any condition that requires reduction of the
permitted emissions.
6.2 The permittee shall pay the annual permit fee invoiced by the Department by the due date stated on
the invoice.
Signed for the Department,
Regional Air Quality Manager, Northwest Region
September 1, 2021
